stem:
Hassan draws line $t$ that crosses lines $p$ and $q$ at two different points. He wants to identify the transversal and organise the angles formed.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: Call the answer "two lines" only, without identifying $t$ as the transversal of $p$ and $q$.
Call $t$ a transversal even if it met only one of $p$ or $q$, skipping that a transversal must intersect two different lines.
$t$ is a transversal of $p$ and $q$; it forms eight angles, with vertically opposite equal pairs at each crossing.
Say that the eight angles are what create transversal $t$, instead of $t$ crossing $p$ and $q$ first.

teacher.key_rationale: A transversal intersects two lines and forms eight angles with vertically opposite equal pairs. Naming only "two lines", dropping the two-line intersection, or reversing angles and transversal all miss that hinge.
